title: Medical AI gains ground in Chinese hospitals
source_used: China Daily, 'Medical AI deepens roots across hospitals' (Borneo Bulletin blocked)
key_facts: More Chinese hospitals are developing their own large language models and embedding AI in daily operations.

East Hospital Affiliated to Tongji University in Shanghai uses Med-Go, a medical LLM built by its doctors; it has been deployed in 46 community health centres in Pudong New Area and at more than 30 major hospitals elsewhere, per the hospital team and local government information.
The hospital is developing more than 40 AI agents for tasks from outpatient consultation to record review; some clinicians first hesitated because responses took 20 to 40 seconds.

West China Hospital in Chengdu built Huaxi Hongyi, whose medical-documentation agent generated more than 1.1 million medical records in 2025, saving more than 300,000 hours of doctors' paperwork time, the hospital said.
IDC estimates China's AI healthcare application software market reached 3.54 billion yuan ($528 million) in 2025 and could reach 14 billion yuan by 2030.
National guidelines call for widespread use of AI-assisted primary care and decision support by 2027; Shanghai targets all medical institutions by 2030.

Obstacles include data fragmentation, privacy concerns and costs; when Med-Go and a doctor disagree the doctor has the final say, though one doctor expects human involvement in some workflows could fall below 10 percent.
quote_evidence: Artificial intelligence is moving deeper into the day-to-day operations of hospitals in China as more medical institutions develop their own large language models and embed AI to improve the quality and efficiency of healthcare services.
Its medical-documentation agent generated more than 1.1 million medical records in 2025, saving more than 300,000 hours of doctors' paperwork time, the hospital said.

why_it_matters_hint: Chinese hospitals are moving medical AI from trials into routine care, but usage figures are the hospitals' own and data sharing and accountability remain open.
